newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer has no plans to spin off drugs unit.
newsitem.headline: Bayer has no plans to spin off drugs unit.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Bayer AG said on Tuesday it was not planning to spin off its drugs unit into a separate legal entity in the medium-term but will continue to look to form joint ventures.

"In the medium-term, the pharma business will stay with us," Bayer management board chairman Manfred Schneider told a news conference, putting to rest speculation that Bayer, like German rival Hoechst AG, is considering a drugs unit spin-off.
While Bayer discussed the option and Schneider said such a step could not be ruled out forever, the group said it will fare better by sticking with its current business structure.
At the same time however, Bayer, which has traditionally preferred to grow through small acquisitions and internal growth, said it remains on the lookout for cooperations and possible partners.

"We continue to be interested in cooperations and mergers as a tool to strengthen our position," Schneider said, adding sometimes several smaller acquisitions may be more interesting than one large takeover.
Schneider said the group was particularly interested in building up its position in Eastern Europe through a number of smaller mergers and cooperations.
Schneider also said a shift of research activities out of Germany would be inevitable as the group builds up research operations in the regions posting the strongest growth rates.
"We will continue to conduct research in Germany but we will also need to be in countries where we sell more," added Bayer board member Walter Wenninger.
Schneider also shrugged off a question that Bayer may plan to merge with its other main German rival BASF AG, saying such discussion were not being held at the moment.
